gate.text: Only someone with access to the server can start setup. Enter the token printed by the installer, or generate a new one on the server with:
gate.tokenHelp: Valid for 1 hour. The browser keeps it only in a secure cookie.
gate.adminExists: An administrator account exists. Sign in as an administrator to continue setup.

language.title: Language
language.help: Default language for setup and the administrator account. You can change it in the panel at any time.

checks.title: System pre-checks
checks.help: Checks the API can verify from its own container: PostgreSQL, Redis, database migrations and the background worker. Operating system, disk and port checks run on the server with "sh scripts/install.sh check".

access.title: Deployment and access address
access.help: The address users will open the panel at. The test checks whether the server can reach itself through this address. Behind NAT a server may not reach its own public address; then the address is saved as unverified.

domain.title: Domain and HTTPS
domain.help: The name the panel will be opened at over HTTPS from the internet. DNS, HTTP reachability and the certificate are tested separately; one passing does not mean the others pass. You can also run without a domain: skip this step and use 127.0.0.1 or an SSH tunnel.

services.title: PostgreSQL and Redis
services.help: The application's database and queue connections. These services run only on the internal Docker network and are never exposed to the internet.

admin.title: Administrator account
admin.help: The first account that manages the panel. After this step the setup token stops working and setup continues only with this account.

vmware.title: ESXi / vCenter connection
vmware.help: The VMware infrastructure the platform will manage virtual servers on. Add a standalone ESXi or a vCenter. vCenter does not replace ESXi; it manages hosts centrally. Do not also add a vCenter-managed host as a standalone ESXi.

discovery.title: Datastore and network discovery
discovery.help: The real hosts, datastores, networks and virtual machines read from the connections.

pools.title: Resource pool and IP plan
pools.help: Capacity and IP ranges to offer for sale or use.

monitoring.title: Monitoring and notifications
monitoring.help: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki and Alertmanager are optional and run in a separate Compose profile. To receive alerts, add a webhook or e-mail receiver to data/observability/alertmanager.yml on the server.

summary.title: Final check and summary
summary.help: Status of each step. Setup cannot finish until required steps are done. Once finished, setup endpoints close; reopening needs "node dist/cli.js recover-setup" on the server.

notAvailable.pools: Resource pools are created in Admin → Catalog; this wizard step comes later.

access.label: Panel address
access.help: Examples: https://panel.example.com or http://127.0.0.1:8080 through an SSH tunnel. Do not add a path, query or user info.

hint.DNS_FAILED: The domain did not resolve. Check that the A record points to the server's public IP and has propagated.
hint.CONNECTION_REFUSED: Connection refused. Check port forwarding, the firewall and the address Caddy listens on (LISTEN_ADDRESS).
hint.TIMEOUT: Timed out. A firewall or NAT may be dropping the connection.
hint.TLS_ERROR: The TLS certificate could not be verified. Do not disable certificate checks; fix the certificate and domain.
hint.WRONG_TARGET: This address answers but is not this installation. DNS or a proxy points to another server.
hint.HTTP_ERROR: The address returned an unexpected HTTP response. A proxy in front may not forward /api to this installation.
hint.LOOPBACK_NOT_VERIFIABLE: 127.0.0.1 and localhost cannot be verified from inside the container. You can save it for use through an SSH tunnel.
hint.UNREACHABLE: The address could not be reached. Check the address and the network path.

admin.done: The administrator account has been created.

monitoring.enable: I will use the monitoring components
monitoring.help: First start the monitoring profile on the server, then test the connection:

summary.warnVmware: No VMware connection configured: the platform cannot create or manage virtual servers yet.
summary.warnAccess: The panel address could not be verified from this server. Open it from another device to check.
summary.warnHttps: HTTPS is not configured. Do not expose the panel to the internet; use 127.0.0.1 or an SSH tunnel, or complete the domain step.

checkCodes.NO_HEARTBEAT: No signal in the last 90 seconds
checkCodes.TLS_ERROR: TLS certificate could not be verified
checkCodes.CERT_STAGING: Let's Encrypt test (staging) certificate; browsers do not trust it

domain.label: Domain name
domain.help: Example: panel.example.com. A subdomain is recommended rather than the bare domain.

howto.dnsRecord: At your DNS provider create an A record for this name pointing to the server's public IPv4 address. Add an AAAA record only if the server has working public IPv6. Do not enter a private address (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x); behind NAT enter your router's public address and forward ports 80/443 to this server.
howto.ports: Ports 80 and 443 must reach this server from the internet: Let's Encrypt validates over 80 (HTTP-01) or 443 (TLS-ALPN-01). If another web server uses these ports, use the 'behind-proxy' mode.
howto.apply: Run the command below on the server. Use --acme-staging first while testing so repeated attempts do not hit real certificate rate limits. Once it works, run it again without that option.
howto.test: Then use 'Test connection' to check DNS, HTTP and the certificate separately. Caddy renews the certificate automatically and keeps it in a persistent volume (caddy_data).

domain.behindProxy: To run behind an existing Nginx/Caddy/Traefik use 'sudo sh scripts/install.sh behind-proxy': the panel listens with plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 and your proxy terminates TLS. Details: docs/domain-https.md
domain.aaaaWarning: This name has an AAAA (IPv6) record. If IPv6 does not really work on the server, remove the record; otherwise some visitors and certificate validation will fail.

hint.DNS_FAILED: The name did not resolve. Create the A record and wait for it to propagate (minutes to hours).
hint.NO_ADDRESS_RECORDS: The name exists but has no A record. Add an A record pointing to the server's public IPv4 address.
hint.CONNECTION_REFUSED: Connection refused: nothing listens on that port. Did you run the installer's 'domain' command? A firewall or port forwarding may block 80/443.
hint.TIMEOUT: Timed out: a firewall or NAT may be dropping the connection. Open 80/443 in your cloud provider's firewall.
hint.HTTP_ERROR: Unexpected HTTP response. A proxy or CDN in front may not forward requests to this installation.
hint.TLS_ERROR: The certificate could not be verified (expired, for another name or self-signed). Do not disable certificate checks; check the domain and Caddy logs: docker compose logs proxy
hint.CERT_STAGING: This is a test certificate. If everything works, run the command again without --acme-staging to get a real certificate.
hint.WRONG_TARGET: This name answers but is not this installation. DNS or a proxy in front points to another server.
hint.UNREACHABLE: The address could not be reached.

vmware.note: The step completes once a connection is added. The detailed inventory is on the VMware page of the admin panel. If you skip this step the platform cannot manage virtual servers.

discovery.none: No connections yet. Go back a step or skip this one.

Vmware.title: ESXi and vCenter connections
Vmware.intro: Real inventory and physical capacity. The platform changes nothing here; it only reads.
Vmware.testOk: Connection succeeded: {kind}. Found {hosts} hosts and {vms} virtual machines. Not saved yet.

form.name: Display name
form.nameHelp: Name shown in the panel, for example 'Frankfurt vCenter'.
form.hostHelp: Management name or IP of the ESXi or vCenter. It must be reachable from the platform server; your browser does not need to reach it.
form.usernameHelp: A dedicated account with the needed privileges is recommended (vCenter example: lightning@vsphere.local).
form.passwordHelp: Stored encrypted; never sent back to the browser and never logged.
form.tlsHelp: Verification is never turned off in any mode.
form.caPemHelp: The vCenter VMCA root certificate or your organisation's CA.
form.sha256Help: Only this exact certificate is accepted. Update it when the certificate is renewed.

cert.title: Presented certificate
cert.explain: This certificate is not trusted yet. Verify the fingerprint on the server itself before connecting.
cert.subject: Subject
cert.pin: I verified the fingerprint, pin this certificate

writeApiNote.restricted: The license looks like the free vSphere Hypervisor: the VMware API is read-only. Server creation and power actions are not possible through this connection.
writeApiNote.unknown: The license could not be read; whether write operations work must be confirmed with a real operation.

warning.HOST_MANAGED_BY_VCENTER: This ESXi is managed by a vCenter. Add the vCenter instead of the host.
warning.LICENSE_UNREADABLE: License information could not be read.
warning.PRIVILEGES_UNREADABLE: The service account's privileges could not be read; operations show as unavailable.

Vmware.capacityNote: Real values of the hosts and datastores. Headroom, capacity offered for sale and reserved capacity are shown per resource pool in Admin → Catalog.

remove.title: Remove connection
remove.explain: Removed only from this panel: the ESXi/vCenter and its virtual machines are not touched. The stored password and inventory are deleted.

Console.title: Console: {name}
Console.osLogin: The console connects to the virtual machine's screen; it does not bypass the operating system's login. A user name and password are still needed.
Console.sdkMissing: The VMware HTML Console SDK is not installed. Its license terms keep it out of this project; download it from Broadcom's developer portal and put these files into the console-sdk/ folder on the server (docs/console.md):

state.error: The console could not be opened

probe.ok: Success: the gateway reached the VM's console endpoint and received data (network path, certificate pinning and ticket work).

reason.CONSOLE_SESSION_INVALID: The console session is invalid, expired or already used. Open the console again.
reason.CONSOLE_REVOKED: The console was closed: the session ended or access was withdrawn.
reason.CONSOLE_EXPIRED: The console reached its maximum duration and was closed. You can open it again.
reason.CONSOLE_LIMIT: The limit of simultaneous consoles was reached. Close another console.
reason.CONSOLE_UNREACHABLE: The console gateway could not reach the VM's host (network access). Check that the panel server can reach the ESXi management network.
reason.CONSOLE_TLS_MISMATCH: The host's certificate did not match the thumbprint VMware reported; the connection was not made, for safety.
reason.CONSOLE_TICKET_REJECTED: The host rejected the console ticket. Open the console again.
reason.CONSOLE_ENDPOINT_BLOCKED: Connecting to the console address VMware returned is not allowed (local or internal network).

Catalog.title: Resource pools and catalog
Catalog.intro: Open existing VMware capacity for sale or use; manage packages, rules, images, IP pools and quotas.
Catalog.poolsExplain: A resource pool creates no physical resources; it opens part of the existing infrastructure's capacity for sale or use. Physical total, management/safety headroom, offered, reserved and really used capacity are shown separately.

warning.STORAGE_FREE_BELOW_HEADROOM: Real free space on the datastores is below the safety headroom.
warning.STORAGE_OVERPROVISIONED: Thin disks promise more than the physical capacity; space may run out as disks fill.
warning.MEMORY_OVERCOMMITTED: RAM assigned to existing VMs exceeds physical RAM.

pools.title: Resource pools
pools.storageNote: Storage: {written} GB written, {provisioned} GB provisioned (thin), real free space {free} GB.
pools.locationHelp: Location name shown to customers (example: Frankfurt).
pools.memoryOvercommitHelp: 1 is recommended; RAM overcommit causes performance problems (1–4).
pools.storageOvercommitHelp: How many times the capacity may be offered with thin disks (1–10).
pools.reserveCpuPctHelp: Management and safety headroom that is never offered.
pools.reserveMemoryPctHelp: Management and safety headroom that is never offered.
pools.reserveStoragePctHelp: Never offered; you are warned when real free space falls below it.

rule.explain: Ranges, steps, allowed RAM per vCPU and unit prices (monthly) customers can choose in this pool.

images.title: Operating system images
images.explain: Images are VM templates in a connection's inventory. The template is prepared in VMware; the platform only selects it here.
images.noTemplates: No templates found in this connection.

ip.title: IP pools
ip.explain: IPv4 only for now. Ranges cannot overlap within one resource pool. Addresses are assigned automatically when a server is created and released after it is deleted.

quotas.title: Quotas
quotas.explain: The default quota applies to everyone; a user quota replaces the default. An empty field is unlimited.

step.readiness: waiting for the operating system to be ready

confirm.power_off: Force off cuts power without telling the operating system; unsaved data may be lost.
confirm.reset: Reset restarts without telling the operating system; unsaved data may be lost.

Servers.powerExplain: Shut down asks the operating system to stop (needs VMware Tools). Force off and reset do not.
Servers.readinessExplain: "Ready": the VM is on, VMware Tools runs and the operating system reports the assigned IP address. A powered-on VM alone is not ready.
Servers.metricsEmpty: No metrics are collected for this server yet. No sample or estimated values are shown.

delete.title: Delete server
delete.explain: The VM is deleted in VMware. The IP address and reserved capacity are released only after VMware confirms the VM is gone. This cannot be undone.

keys.title: SSH keys
keys.explain: Public keys are installed on the server with cloud-init. SSH password login is created disabled.
keys.name: Key name

admin.title: Servers and operations
admin.intro: All servers, automation jobs, failed operations and reconciliation with VMware.
admin.reconcileExplain: Compares the platform's records with the real state in VMware. It reports findings; it never deletes anything by itself.
admin.search: Search by name, owner, IP or pool

Maintenance.title: Backups and updates
Maintenance.settings: Scheduled maintenance: {schedule} · keep {keep} local backups · external copy: {copy} · automatic update: {auto} (channel {channel}, window {window})
Maintenance.explain: Backups, restores and updates run on the server with scripts/install.sh (backup, restore, update, schedule, auto-update). The panel only shows their results. Backups hold the panel's own data, not customer VMs; a VMware snapshot is not a backup.

code.E_BACKUP_KEY_MISSING: the backup key secrets/backup.key is missing
code.E_BACKUP_DB: the database could not be dumped
code.E_BACKUP_VERIFY: the backup file could not be read back (disk full?)
code.E_BACKUP_COPY: written locally but not copied to the external target
code.E_RESTORE_DB: the database could not be restored
code.E_RESTORE_START: data restored but the services did not become ready
code.E_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE: that version lacks a migration already applied (no database downgrade)
code.E_UPDATE_FAILED: the new version did not become ready
code.W_UPDATE_BUSY: operations were running; tried again in the next hour
